title: Evening — What To Do With It
summary: One free slice and more than one slice's worth of leads. Put the options on the board and make them choose out loud. This is the campaign's core economy and this is the session it should first bite.

beats.text: Five leads on the board, one slice between them. They can do one. Six players will want three.
beats.direction: Let them argue. Do not rescue them from the choice.

beats.text: They commit. Note which four they did not take — leads decay differently, and that record is the whole point of making them choose out loud.
Whoever holds the lens from Session Four looks through it. Only that player is told anything.
beats.direction: Do not confirm or deny anything afterward. If the table asks whether the lens is broken, the honest GM answer is a shrug.

when.condition: only if they spent the slice on the lens

beats.note: The cleanest single-player moment in the chapter. On a critical success give them a full paragraph and let the table wonder why one person has gone quiet.

gmModifiers.label: The lens — local density
gmModifiers.note: NEVER show this to the player, and never tell them the DC. The lens works perfectly and always has — its apparent unreliability is entirely about what is or is not in the room. Chapter One weighting is +0 to +2 almost everywhere; the Founding Day square in Session Six is +8 and they will not have brought it. Building a false theory about when it works is the point: Manako spent six years doing exactly this.

offers.name: Chandlers on the harbour side
offers.effect: Who buys marine primer in quantity — and one name that recurs.

offers.name: Follow up on Kudo
offers.effect: Shinobu's situation, from the only person who will describe it honestly.

offers.name: The lens
offers.effect: Look through it properly, somewhere chosen rather than somewhere convenient.

offers.name: Nozomi's locker
offers.effect: It has not been cleared. Somebody is still paying the fee on it.

offers.name: Anchor time
offers.effect: Whatever their own life needs tonight.

carryForward: Which of the five leads they took, and which four they declined.
Every lens roll, with the hidden modifier, so the pattern is reconstructable later.
notes: expiresOn is null on all five because this episode's dayRange is not yet placed and a moment key is absolute ("d9:evening"). The decay is authored in prose for now — the chandler will still be there next week, Kudo's mood will not — and the real keys go in when the episode lands on a day. Worth knowing this is a genuine gap: an episode written before it is scheduled cannot express relative expiry.
